summary: Environment A evidence for replacing LocalAcousticMusicRecognizer's honest Phase 2.2 scaffold with a real, offline spectral landmark (constellation) hashing audio fingerprinting algorithm.
auditFinding: integrations/music-acoustic's LocalAcousticMusicRecognizer always reported Unavailable/Error - Phase 2.2 deliberately left no fingerprint algorithm implemented, only the real configuration/status-resolution boundary and a documented seam (recognize()'s RecognitionFailed branch). No acoustic recognition algorithm existed anywhere in the codebase. See docs/phase-7-audit.md and docs/phase-7-1-real-audio-fingerprinting.md.
designChoice: No genuine architectural fork - the seam, manifest convention, and desktop wiring already existed and required zero changes. The one real decision was which algorithm: spectral landmark hashing (Wang 2003, the published Shazam algorithm) - offline, well-understood, testable on synthetic signals, pure-Rust-implementable with no native toolchain dependency.

newCode.fingerprintRs: integrations/music-acoustic/src/fingerprint.rs (new): fingerprint() extracts spectral-peak landmark hashes via rustfft STFT; FingerprintIndex enrolls reference clips and matches query clips via hash lookup + offset-histogram voting.
newCode.localRs: integrations/music-acoustic/src/local.rs (rewritten): LocalAcousticMusicRecognizer::configure() parses an extended manifest ({songs: [{songId, contentId, audioPath}]}), reads each WAV file via hound, downmixes to mono, and enrolls into a real FingerprintIndex. recognize() queries the index and maps votes to a capped ConfidenceResult.
newCode.dependencies: rustfft (pure-Rust FFT) and hound (pure-Rust WAV codec) added to integrations/music-acoustic/Cargo.toml only - neither requires a C/C++ toolchain.

coverage: a clip matches itself with a strong majority vote at one offset
two acoustically different synthetic songs do not cross-match
a cropped mid-clip excerpt still matches via time-shift invariance
moderate added white noise still matches
silence and an empty index produce zero matches, never fabricated
min-votes threshold correctly filters weak/coincidental matches
enrolling the same song twice is additive
hash packing is lossless for realistic inputs
the full manifest -> WAV file -> real FingerprintIndex -> recognize() round trip, with real (test-generated) WAV files via hound
content_id dataset scoping is honored even for a real acoustic match
one bad reference file in a manifest does not prevent other songs from enrolling
every prior Phase 2.2 status-resolution test (disabled/no-dir/nonexistent-dir/empty-manifest/malformed-manifest) still passes unchanged

fullRegression.fmt: cargo fmt --all -- --check: clean (after one cargo fmt --all pass)
fullRegression.clippy: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean, both feature configs
fullRegression.check: cargo check --workspace: clean, both with and without --features whisper,semantic-search
fullRegression.test: cargo test --workspace: all crates passing, both feature configs, zero regressions outside cip-integrations-music-acoustic
fullRegression.frontend: npm run typecheck/lint/test/build: all clean/unchanged - zero frontend files touched this phase; 258/258 tests still pass, lint shows the same 5 pre-existing warnings as before

architecturalSafetyNotes: Zero new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new database schema - the entire change sits behind AcousticMusicRecognizer, a trait wired end to end since Phase 2.2.

core/music (the domain contract crate) is untouched - the algorithm lives entirely in integrations/music-acoustic, honoring the project's own boundary rule that core crates never depend on a specific implementation.
NullAcousticMusicRecognizer and ScriptedAcousticMusicRecognizer are byte-identical to before this phase.
A build with no manifest configured (the default, every shipped build today) behaves identically to every prior phase - Unavailable, never fabricated recognition.
honestLimitation: No real recorded audio exists anywhere in this repository or container to enroll or query against - the algorithm is proven correct on synthetic multi-tone signals only. Its real-world false-positive/false-negative behavior against actual congregational singing, live instrumentation, and room acoustics is genuinely unknown until Environment C testing with real reference recordings happens.
